findings.title: unsubscribe crashes with NoMethodError when no TopicUser row exists
findings.body: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return nil, and the very next line calls `tu.notification_level`, producing a 500. Not every emailed user has a topic_users row: mailing-list-mode emails (`mailing_list_notify`) are sent to users who may never have visited the topic, so the per-topic unsubscribe link added to those emails (`unsubscribe_url: post.topic.unsubscribe_url`) will 500 for exactly the users most likely to click it. Use `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic_id, notification_level: ...)` which creates the row if missing, or handle the nil case.

findings.title: unsubscribe bypasses TopicUser.change, skipping reason tracking and MessageBus notification
findings.body: The action mutates `tu.notification_level` directly and calls `tu.save!` instead of `TopicUser.change`. `TopicUser.change` sets `notifications_changed_at` and `notifications_reason_id` (:user_changed) and publishes `notification_level_change` over MessageBus. Bypassing it means (a) other open browser tabs/devices never learn of the change in real time, and (b) because `notifications_reason_id` stays null, auto-track logic (`TopicUser.auto_track` and the auto-track branch in `update_last_read`) can silently flip the user's level back to tracking the next time they read the topic, undoing the unsubscribe.

findings.title: State-changing unsubscribe performed on a plain GET request
findings.body: The new `GET /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe` route immediately mutes/regularizes the topic for the logged-in user as a side effect of rendering the page. GET links in emails are routinely pre-fetched by mail scanners and link-protection services (e.g. Outlook SafeLinks, corporate proxies), so a user can have a topic muted without ever clicking anything. Unsubscribe links should land on a confirmation page and perform the state change via POST/PUT (as the site's existing email unsubscribe flow does with a key + POST), or at minimum only apply the change after explicit user confirmation.

findings.title: unsubscribe_url ignores relative_root / subfolder installs incorrectly in redirect
findings.body: `unsubscribe_url` is built as `"#{url}/unsubscribe"` where `url` uses `Discourse.base_url` (no `Discourse.base_uri` path handling issue for emails, which is fine), but in `TopicsController#unsubscribe` it is also used for the 301 slug-redirect (`redirect_to @topic_view.topic.unsubscribe_url`). Redirecting to the absolute URL is acceptable, but the redirect condition `(!request.format.json? && params[:slug].blank?)` combined with this absolute URL means the no-slug route `/t/:topic_id/unsubscribe` issues a redirect on every email click before doing the work — harmless but an extra hop; more importantly the JSON-format branch never redirects even when the slug is wrong, so the state change happens on mismatched-slug API calls.
